en.title: Slice the banana
en.description: Cut the banana into large chunks and place them directly into the blender bowl.

en.title: Add cranberries and honey
en.description: Toss in the fresh cranberries and drizzle in the honey to sweeten the blend.

en.title: Pour in the kefir
en.description: Add the chilled kefir to the blender bowl to create the liquid base for your smoothie.

en.title: Blend until combined
en.description: Blend on medium speed for 2 to 3 minutes until you achieve a smooth consistency with small cranberry fragments.

en.title: Serve immediately
en.description: Pour the finished smoothie into tall glasses, add straws, and serve right away for the best flavor.

en.title: Sauté the spinach
en.description: Melt half the butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the spinach and cook for 3 minutes until wilted. Transfer to a plate.

en.title: Chop the spinach
en.description: Once the spinach has cooled slightly, chop it finely with a knife and set aside.

en.title: Prepare the bread, cheese and garlic
en.description: Cut the crusts off the bread slices and dice the crumb into 2 cm cubes. Grate the cheese and mince the garlic clove.

en.title: Whisk the egg mixture
en.description: In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, cream, salt, black pepper and paprika until smooth.

en.title: Combine spinach, cheese and garlic with eggs
en.description: Add the chopped spinach, grated cheese and minced garlic to the egg mixture. Stir gently until evenly distributed.

en.title: Pour egg mixture over bread and let soak
en.description: Pour the egg mixture over the bread cubes and stir gently to coat all pieces. Let it soak for 15 minutes, allowing the bread to absorb the liquid.

en.title: Grease the dish and transfer the mixture
en.description: Grease a baking dish with the remaining butter. Transfer the soaked bread mixture into the dish and pour any leftover egg mixture on top.

en.title: Bake the omelette
en.description: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Place the dish in the oven and bake for 15 minutes until the omelette is set and golden. Serve warm, garnished with cilantro if desired.

en.title: Boil water
en.description: Bring a small amount of water to a boil. This will be used to dissolve the instant coffee.

en.title: Dissolve instant coffee
en.description: Pour the boiling water over the instant coffee and stir until fully dissolved.

en.title: Break ladyfingers into pieces
en.description: Break the ladyfinger biscuits into pieces about 3–4 cm in size.

en.title: Dip biscuits in coffee
en.description: Quickly dip each biscuit piece into the prepared coffee mixture. Do not soak too long or they will become too soft.

en.title: Combine coffee with yogurt
en.description: Pour the remaining coffee into the Greek yogurt and stir until smooth and homogeneous.

en.title: Divide yogurt mixture into glasses
en.description: Evenly distribute the yogurt-coffee mixture between two serving glasses.

en.title: Insert biscuits into yogurt
en.description: Insert the dipped biscuit pieces into the yogurt mixture, pressing them in slightly. Some pieces may stick out, that's fine.

en.title: Refrigerate for 3 hours
en.description: Place the glasses in the refrigerator and chill for at least 3 hours, preferably overnight. The biscuits will absorb moisture and the dessert will set.

en.title: Grate beets and garlic
en.description: Coarsely grate the beetroot and press the garlic clove through a press. Place the prepared vegetables in a bowl.

en.title: Blend the beet mixture
en.description: Add the ricotta, water, olive oil and salt to the bowl. Use an immersion blender to blend everything into a smooth puree.

en.title: Spread beet mixture on bread
en.description: Generously spread the beet mixture onto 2 slices of toast bread. Sprinkle with arugula.

en.title: Cover and cut the sandwich
en.description: Top with the remaining 2 slices of bread. Cut the sandwiches diagonally.

en.title: Add oats to egg whites
en.description: Add the quick-cooking oats to the egg whites and stir gently.

en.title: Mash banana
en.description: Mash half a banana with a fork until smooth.

en.title: Whisk the batter
en.description: Add the banana puree and milk to the oat mixture. Whisk with a whisk or mixer until smooth and uniform.

en.title: Add cinnamon and vanilla
en.description: Add ground cinnamon and vanilla. Mix well.

en.title: Rest the batter
en.description: Let the batter rest at room temperature for 10 minutes to allow the oats to absorb liquid and swell.

en.title: Heat the pan
en.description: Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Brush or lightly oil the surface with vegetable oil.

en.title: Pour the batter
en.description: Pour all the batter into the skillet and spread it evenly to form one large pancake.

en.title: Cook first side
en.description: Cook the pancake for 3–4 minutes, until the bottom is golden brown and set. Do not rush; medium heat ensures even cooking.

en.title: Flip the pancake
en.description: Drizzle a small amount of oil over the top of the pancake, then carefully flip it with a spatula.

en.title: Cook second side
en.description: Cook the other side for 1–2 minutes, until golden brown.

en.title: Transfer to plate
en.description: Slide the finished oat pancake onto a serving plate.
